title: Introduce multitenant commitment simulator and deferred surge auditor
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Adds a lightweight multitenant commitment simulator (pkg/autoscaler/simulator) and a deferred surge auditor (pkg/auditor) that records late-arriving bursts against provisioned commitments.
Motivation: We continue to see production surprises when short, missed-enforcement surges interact with long commitment windows — apps observe transient degradation even though aggregate capacity was sufficient. This PR provides two tools: (1) a simulator that replays real tenant request traces against configurable commitment/window policies to expose under-covered surge patterns, and (2) an auditor that runs in the control plane to detect deferred surges (requests served after a commitment tick but attributable to earlier windows) and emit corrective telemetry and optional enforcement suggestions.
Scope:
- New simulator binary cmd/mcs/sim that accepts trace CSV/Parquet and policy YAML and emits windowed coverage heatmaps and summary metrics.
- Control-plane auditor that annotates tenant utilization reports with deferred-surge counters and suggested credit-reconciliation actions.
- Small runtime hook (autoscaler/controller) to surface aggregated deferred-surge ratios for a tenant in the console.
- End-to-end tests and a docs page with sample workflows and remediation guidance.
Description (long): The simulator allows SREs and capacity planners to run what-if scenarios against commit-window sizes, soft/hard reservation envelopes, and different traffic burst models (poisson, heavy-tail, replayed traces). The outputs include per-window shortfall histograms, tail percentile of burst overlap, and an exported CSV that the auditor can consume. The deferred-surge auditor observes historical request timings and uses the same window attribution logic as the simulator to flag cases where requests were admitted in a later window but originated (by timestamp) in an earlier one, which can happen due to queueing, preemption fallbacks, or transient provisioning delays.
The auditor:
- tags tenant reports with deferred_surge_count and deferred_surge_ratio
- produces suggested actions (e.g., increase warm pool, raise soft reservation, or temporary burst-grant)
- exposes Prometheus metrics redwood_deferred_surge_ratio{tenant="..."} and a per-tenant histogram for surge sizes
Checklists and acceptance criteria:
- [x] simulator binary that runs on local traces and outputs CSV/JSON summary
- [x] auditor component with unit tests and integration test that runs against a trace fixture
- [x] telemetry added and wired to console dashboard (backend + basic frontend flag)
- [x] docs page under docs/operating/dedicated/commitments.md
- [x] e2e scenario exercises a synthetic delayed-provision path
Implementation notes:
- The simulator is intentionally single-threaded for deterministic replay; it supports a --workers flag but defaults to one to make diffs reproducible.
- Attribution uses an inclusive windowing rule: request belongs to the window of its arrival timestamp; if admitted in a later window, it is marked deferred.
- Auditor runs as a best-effort background job in the control plane; it does not change admission decisions in this PR (enforcement is a follow-up).
Commits (high level):
- commit 1: add simulator core (+trace parsers, simple policy YAML)
- commit 2: wire up CSV/Parquet input and sample trace fixtures
- commit 3: add deferred surge auditor and Prometheus metrics
- commit 4: console telemetry wiring and docs
- commit 5: e2e tests and CI fixes
Files changed (high level):
- pkg/autoscaler/simulator.go: new simulator engine and attribution windowing
- cmd/mcs/main.go: CLI for running local replays and exporting summaries
- pkg/auditor/surge_auditor.go: deferred surge detection, tagging, and export hooks
- pkg/telemetry/metrics.go: added deferred_surge metrics and labels
- internal/console/telemetry_integration.go: basic backend plumbing and feature flag
- docs/operating/dedicated/commitments.md: operational runbook and sample remediation
- test/e2e/fixtures/delayed_provision_trace.parquet: synthetic trace
- charts/dedicated/templates/auditor-deployment.yaml: k8s manifest for auditor
- Makefile/CI: new e2e target and small lint rule updates
Review notes and comments:
- Tomás Rivera (review): "Nice shape. Simulator design looks straightforward. Two asks: (1) clarify invariants for attribution when clocks skew between router and control plane, (2) please add a small benchmark to show simulator runtime with 1M events." -> Author reply: "Added a section to docs about clock skew handling and implemented a simple --timestamp-offset flag for the simulator; added a micro-benchmark in test/sim_bench_test.go with 1M-event run and CI target (fast)."
- Liam Chen (request changes): "Auditor should avoid high-cardinality labels on the deferred_surge histogram. Can we aggregate by tenant tier instead of raw tenant id in histograms?" -> Author reply: "Changed histogram labels to tenant_tier and kept tenant_id only on counter joins (sparse). Updated metrics.go and tests."
- Nora Patel (approve): "Approach looks good; appreciate docs and runbook. Approved pending CI green."
CI history:
- Initial CI: unit tests failed (simulator parsing edge-case with zero-length trace)
- Fix applied in commit 4 and test added
- Subsequent CI: unit + lint passed, e2e target initially flaky (timing), re-run passed
- Final status: all checks green (unit/lint/e2e/bench).
Performance and safety considerations:
- Simulator is non-blocking and CLI-only; it does not touch production state.
- Auditor runs read-only analysis for this PR and writes only aggregated counters; no admission side-effects.
- Prometheus metrics are namespaced and rate-limited to avoid cardinality explosions.
Documentation and runbook:
- docs/operating/dedicated/commitments.md includes how to run local replays, interpret heatmaps, recommended remediation (warm pool sizing, soft reservation tuning, suggested temporary grants), and an example Linear ticket template for follow-up changes.
Migration and follow-ups:
- Follow-up work includes: (A) enforcement mode where the auditor can propose automated reconcilers, (B) console UI to visualize per-tenant deferred surge timelines, (C) a tenant-facing notification that explains temporary credits.
Release notes:
- Added simulator to aid capacity planning; added auditor to detect deferred surges and emit telemetry for remediation.
Merge and deployment notes:
- Merged to main via squash on 2026-02-02 (commit sha: f3a9e2d).
- Auditor will be deployed behind a feature flag and rolled to staging for two weeks before enabling in prod.
Contact: aisha@redwood.ai for follow-ups and runbook questions.

release_notes: Add multitenant commitment simulator for replaying traces and a deferred-surge auditor that emits per-tenant deferred surge telemetry and suggested remediation. No enforcement changes in this release; auditor is read-only and feature-flagged.
notes_for_ops: Deploy auditor behind feature flag; monitor redwood_deferred_surge_ratio and CPU/Memory of auditor pod. Roll to staging for 2 weeks before enabling read-only alerts in prod.
examples: Run simulator: ./mcs sim --trace delayed_provision_trace.parquet --policy sample_policy.yaml --out summary.csv
Check metrics: query rate() of redwood_deferred_surge_ratio by tenant_tier over 5m
additional_context: This PR came from ENG-4125 (capacity planning) after a support incident SUP-8783 where a large customer experienced queued requests that were admitted in subsequent windows. The simulator helped reproduce the incident locally and informed suggested warm pool increases.
